The core operators form a layered logical architecture: the duplicate gate (D) ensures no redundant contest artifacts are created by checking against a set of matched IDs (M), enforcing a dependency chain. The fake data constraint (F) isolates the system from real-world data contamination through a boolean flag. The legal boundary enforcement (L) acts as a risk filter that blocks high-impact contest types unless explicit approval is granted. These primitives interact in a hierarchical manner: D must resolve before F can be applied, and both must satisfy L before any real-world interaction occurs. Failure modes arise when dependencies are ignored (D=false), real data is imported without consent (R=true, F=false), or high-risk activities proceed without approval (L=false). The system's robustness depends on these constraints forming a closed-loop feedback mechanism.
